researched.reason: Admach Systems Ltd (BSE SME 544669), market cap Rs 352.2 cr, close Rs 520.0 on 15-Oct-2026. Two filings today, both opened: (a) a Reg 30 intimation of a purchase order of Rs 791.80 lakh INCLUDING GST from 'a renowned listed domestic company in the steel industry' for processing and NDT equipment for steel bars, 26 weeks to execute, paid 20% against an advance bank guarantee / 70% against inspection / 10% after commissioning against a 12-month performance bank guarantee, no promoter interest and not a related-party transaction; and (b) a press release stating 'current order book stands at Rs 76.25 crore, including GST'. THREE MEASURED REASONS NOT TO PUBLISH, each from a document read this run. 1. THE ORDER BOOK HAS NOT GROWN. The company publishes a 'Total Order Book' press release with almost every order, and the series it has itself stated is: Rs 76.25 cr on 08-Jun-2026 -> Rs 68.37 cr on 18-Aug-2026 -> Rs 69.04 cr on 30-Sep-2026 -> Rs 76.25 cr on 15-Oct-2026. Today's headline reads like growth; the book is EXACTLY the figure of four months ago, and was lower in between. Execution is consuming the book about as fast as new orders arrive. 2. IT IS A SERIAL ORDER FILER, THE WORST BUCKET IN THE STUDY. Order-receipt announcements since listing: 11-Mar, 06-Jun, 24-Jun, 06-Jul, 15-Jul, 14-Aug, 30-Sep and 15-Oct-2026 - EIGHT in about seven months, each with its own order-book press release. The 2026-09-22 study of 1,245 order filings (runbook 144c) found a company with eight or more prior order filings reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and 5x NEVER, against 30.4% / 3.5% for a first-in-two-years filer. 3. THE ORDER IS TOO SMALL AGAINST SALES, WHICH IS THE RATIO THAT PREDICTS. FY26 audited revenue Rs 68.91 cr, PAT Rs 10.01 cr (BSE detailed results). Rs 7.918 cr including GST is about 11.5% of a year's sales - the under-25% bucket, which reached 2x 21.4% of the time against 35.7% for the 25-50% bucket. The whole order book is only 1.1x FY26 revenue. Two further facts for the record: median daily turnover is Rs 19.4 lakh, BELOW the playbook's Rs 25 lakh liquidity floor; and BSE's header puts the stock on PE 35.18 (EPS 14.78) after +149.5% in six months, so the re-rating has largely happened. Also noted, not researched further: the CFO resigned on 16-May-2026, and on 29-Sep-2026 the company filed a clarification about its own earlier 'Change in Management' disclosure.

ArMee Infotech Ltd (BSE 544951 / NSE ARMEE), market cap Rs 815.7 cr, close Rs 257.05. Scan trigger was RESULT x2 - the board approved, on 15-Oct-2026, the unaudited results for the quarter ended 30-JUNE-2026, i.e. Q1 FY27 reported three and a half months late (the company listed in 2026 after a Rs 300 cr fresh issue at Rs 375 a share). Read from the filed statement (standalone, Rs lakh): revenue from operations 27,326.70 for the quarter to 30-Jun-2026 against 27,028.90 for the quarter to 30-Jun-2025 - **+1.1% YoY**; PAT 276.85 against 95.27 - +190% YoY but off a Rs 0.95 cr base; FY26 (audited) revenue 1,45,583.33 (Rs 1,455.8 cr) and PAT 5,126.74 (Rs 51.3 cr), EPS 21.60. NOT PUBLISHED. The playbook's results trigger needs revenue growth of 30% or more YoY with PAT growth; +1.1% fails it outright. The profit jump is not evidence of a turn either: the business is heavily back-ended - the quarter to 31-Mar-2026 alone did revenue of 89,329.52 lakh (Rs 893.3 cr) of the Rs 1,455.8 cr year and PAT of Rs 50.2 cr - so a Q1 at Rs 273 cr and Rs 2.8 cr says little about FY27. The same board outcome also discloses a proposal to raise up to Rs 450 cr through secured listed NCDs on private placement, 'still under consideration', with due diligence pending and no use of proceeds stated: Rs 450 cr of debt against a Rs 816 cr market capitalisation, which is the kind of unspecified fund raise the playbook says to skip rather than model.
